evp.title: FinTech Client: shared QA platform
evp.lead: A payment-release story for a fictional fintech with 75 offshore QA staff.
evp.note: Executive briefing • Strategic vision • Client scenario

evp.title: The QA organization
evp.lead: Five application squads share 75 offshore QA staff. Each person appears in one primary-role group.
evp.note: The pilot draws eight QA staff from this population. Headcount alone does not establish a savings opportunity.

evp.title: QE testing scenario: one timeout, two debits
evp.lead: PAY-142 simulates a CAD 100 transfer accepted before a timeout. The customer retries; an injected duplicate-posting defect tests whether QE catches the second debit.
evp.note: Expected: one transfer, one balanced journal and one customer-visible result. This is a QE test scenario, not a reported client incident.

evp.title: Where the release work goes
evp.lead: Modelled hands-on effort for one bounded release test pack. Eight stages add to 300 hours.
evp.note: The pack spans 10 business days. Waiting time and human effort use different units and must be measured separately.

evp.title: The platform investment
evp.lead: Common context, fixtures and evidence serve every squad. Application teams retain business ownership.
evp.note: Existing test frameworks and pipelines execute approved work. AI supports preparation and interpretation.

evp.title: AI assistance across the release
evp.note: The same 75-person organization gains reusable capability. Client effort, waiting and value remain to be measured.

evp.title: Delivery maturity changes the first move
evp.lead: The same tool creates different work in a shared manual environment and a repeatable delivery system.
evp.note: These profiles illustrate effort, not adoption approval. Review twelve dependency areas before committing to scope, dates or benefits.

evp.title: What 78 hours of gross capacity means
evp.lead: Mixed-maturity target: 300 hours becomes 222, including 40 hours of review.
evp.note: Conditional capacity arithmetic; adoption prerequisites are unverified. Tool, cloud and vendor charges are excluded. This is not cash ROI or measured AI impact.

evp.title: Ownership within the offshore model
rows: Shared enablement
Own context adapters, templates, fixtures, runner integration and coaching.
Application QA teams
Own business scenarios, expected results, execution and defect disposition.
Product and release owners
Resolve requirement questions and accept the release evidence.
Delivery management
Provide repository access, overlap hours and an explicit backlog for freed capacity.
evp.note: Reskill domain testers through paired reviews. Agree supplier incentives and reuse ownership before scaling.

evp.title: A proposed twelve-week engagement
evp.lead: A measured pilot creates a reusable delivery pattern and a decision about the next applications.
evp.note: Infrastructure, provider access, data and reviewer capacity can extend a phase. Re-estimate remediation before committing to this illustrative schedule.

evp.title: The evidence needed to expand
rows: Quality
All mandatory payment assertions pass; no unexplained skips or weakened checks.
Effort
Include preparation, review, correction, retesting and platform operation.
Delivery
Report elapsed time, waiting reasons and failed-run recovery separately.
Reuse
A second squad runs the pattern and maintains it without the pilot authors.
evp.note: A faster draft is insufficient. Compare tasks of similar scope and retain conventional work as a reference.

evp.title: The senior-director conversation
points: “Across the 75 QA staff, where do people spend time and where are they waiting?”
“Which payment journey has stable requirements, observable outcomes and an owner who can join a pilot?”
“Could one platform team remove duplicated work across the squads?”
“If we return capacity, which backlog or release commitment will use it?”
evp.note: Proposed next step: a workflow assessment with the QA, development and platform leads. Agree a bounded pilot after reviewing the baseline.

evp.title: Adoption depends on funded foundations
evp.note: FinTech Client has not been assessed. The dependency backlog can change scope, cost and timing; the 480-hour setup allowance is not a client quote.

evp.title: Modernization enables wider AI adoption
evp.note: For FinTech Client, fund repeatable payment tests and shared QE services alongside reviewed AI assistance. Validate this capability roadmap through client discovery.

evp.title: Peer evidence for the payments pilot
evp.note: Peer results support a trial. Outcomes for FinTech Client remain unmeasured.

evp.title: FinTech Client: where to begin
evp.note: Choose one entry point, validate its prerequisites and agree how reviewers will judge the result. Wider rollout depends on local evidence.

technical.title: FinTech Client: QA architecture
technical.lead: A concrete design for AI assistance across a release workflow with 75 offshore QA staff.
technical.note: Technical SDs and leads • Fictional fintech • Proposed architecture

technical.title: The application landscape
technical.lead: Payment APIs offer the first controlled test surface. Other applications follow their own readiness.
technical.note: Example stack: Java/Spring Boot, React, PostgreSQL and Azure. Existing automation remains useful.

technical.title: The shared QA platform
technical.lead: The model proposes artifacts. Reviewers approve them. Existing runners produce evidence.
technical.note: Adapters, context assembly and evidence linking are integration work to build. No turnkey platform is implied.

technical.title: PAY-142: the payment contract
rows: Same key + same payload
Return the same transfer ID and result. Post the journal once.
Same key + changed amount
Reject the conflicting request without another posting.
Concurrent retries / duplicate callbacks
Converge on one transfer and one balanced journal.
Expected final state
Payer CAD 900.00; recipient CAD 100.00; one journal with two balancing entries.
technical.note: Authored business rules: initial balances CAD 1,000.00 and CAD 0.00; transfer CAD 100.00; no fees, FX or other activity. No regulatory claim.

technical.title: QE testing scenario: detecting a duplicate posting
technical.lead: Simulate an accepted transfer, a timed-out response and a retry. A deliberately injected defect posts the same transfer twice.
technical.note: Assert one journal and correct balances. The duplicate-posting variant must fail. This is a QE test scenario, not a reported client incident.

technical.title: Requirements and test design
technical.lead: PAY-142 starts with an ambiguity: does a timeout mean failure, success or unknown?
technical.note: Domain QA and the product owner approve expected behavior before generated tests can validate it.

technical.title: Test data and environment preparation
technical.lead: Synthetic accounts, known balances and a controlled provider response make the retry repeatable.
technical.note: Container-based service tests do not replace real integration, mobile or batch testing. Validate stubs against the provider contract.

technical.title: Generated code enters an ordinary review
technical.lead: Use the approved case matrix and repository examples to produce a candidate test change.
technical.note: The reviewer checks the oracle. A deliberate duplicate-posting fault must fail before the candidate joins the required suite.

technical.title: The appropriate test layer
rows: Service and API
REST Assured + JUnit. Cover retry, concurrent requests, idempotency conflicts and journal outcomes.
Web journey
Playwright for the new React flow. Check pending state, retry action and the final customer message.
Existing browser and mobile
Keep owned Selenium and Appium coverage. Change frameworks only when maintenance evidence supports it.
Batch and integration
Retain settlement-file reconciliation and provider sandbox checks with explicit scheduling.
technical.note: Test distribution follows behavior and observability. A new browser framework does not solve a shared settlement environment.

technical.title: Execution retains required coverage
technical.lead: CI records the build, fixture, stub and test revisions before runners execute the pack.
technical.note: AI test-selection recommendations run in shadow mode first. Required payment checks continue on every eligible release.

technical.title: Triage preserves the original test intent
technical.lead: A failed journal assertion belongs to the product defect path until evidence establishes otherwise.
technical.note: Capture failed tests, skipped tests and retries. A repair that removes an assertion does not count as a passing outcome.

technical.title: A traceable release decision
technical.lead: Every generated artifact and run links back to the approved business behavior.
technical.note: An absent result remains unknown. The release owner resolves exceptions and the QA lead reviews the evidence pack.

technical.title: What the demonstration proves
rows: Normal transfer
One posting and expected balances: the modeled checks pass.
Retry with injected bug
Two postings and incorrect balances: the modeled checks block release.
Retry with deduplication
One posting after two attempts: the modeled checks pass.
Duplicate callback
Repeat the event with the same identity and inspect the journal outcome.
technical.note: The browser demonstration is a deterministic teaching model. It does not execute REST Assured, call a payment service or prove production correctness.

technical.title: Readiness across six dimensions
technical.lead: These dimensions describe the delivery profile in this scenario. Review the wider dependency register before approving a workflow.
technical.note: Assess each application separately. Unknown infrastructure, data, virtualization, AI access or ownership must be resolved before the affected workflow can proceed.

technical.title: Offshore handoff and platform ownership
technical.lead: Each handoff carries a reproducible artifact and a named next owner.
technical.note: Pilot team: one QA lead, four domain testers, two automation engineers and one data/environment engineer. Product, development and platform support contribute separately.

technical.title: Effort includes review and operation
technical.lead: Record time at the eight workflow stages using the same boundary for baseline and assisted packs.
technical.note: Targets assume verified adoption prerequisites. Negative capacity remains possible; do not extrapolate one pack to all 75 staff or combine overlapping benefits.

technical.title: Pilot validation and stop conditions
rows: Design
Baseline one current pack. Compare at least two assisted packs with similar scope and matched conventional tasks.
Record
Capture task complexity, reviewer time, corrections, failures, waits and environment incidents.
Stop or repair
Pause expansion for an escaped money-movement defect, unreliable fixtures or tests that pass the injected fault.
Expand
Require trustworthy mandatory coverage, positive net capacity and a successful second-squad reuse trial.
technical.note: Small pilot samples support a delivery decision with uncertainty. They do not establish a general causal productivity rate.

technical.title: Architecture questions for the leads
points: “Can we deploy a known build, reset the data and replay a provider timeout today?”
“Where do payment outcomes become observable: API, journal, callback or batch file?”
“Which framework already has maintainers and reliable CI execution?”
“Who owns reusable fixtures and who approves the expected financial behavior?”
technical.note: Review the workflow map and a real failed release together. The first implementation backlog should follow those answers.

technical.title: Platform prerequisites for the pilot
technical.note: Unknown evidence remains a gap. Platform owners, reviewers and supplier leads must accept named actions and review dates before adoption.

technical.title: Service virtualization and real integration
technical.lead: Control the payment provider for repeatable tests; keep a separate real-integration gate.
technical.note: WireMock is an HTTP example. Contract fidelity, callback behavior and batch access need explicit owners; passing a stub does not prove end-to-end correctness.

technical.title: FinTech Client: test environment
technical.note: The CI runner checks the real payment service and database against reviewed provider models. Retain separate provider and settlement evidence.

technical.title: Technology roles in the payment pilot
technical.note: Choose Testcontainers, Compose or an existing supported environment for the test scope. Mobile devices and legacy settlement retain their own integration requirements.

technical.title: A candidate test must earn acceptance
technical.note: PAY-142 must catch an incorrect transfer, journal or balance. The guided example rejects the candidate and leaves the maintained suite unchanged.

technical.title: A fair comparison for the payments pilot
technical.note: Use comparable tasks inside the proposed pilot. Include failures and review effort; retain the existing mandatory payment checks.

technical.title: The runtime from setup to cleanup
technical.note: Repeatable execution is a platform capability. Retain failure evidence and attempt cleanup on every path; real integration remains separate.

technical.title: Connect the tools behind the platform
technical.note: Proposed integration. Validate access; fund context adapters and joined evidence.
